name: Paradev (formerly Superset)
title: Ninebrains vs Paradev (formerly Superset)
description: Ninebrains vs Paradev, the parallel coding-agent app formerly called Superset: licence, platforms, isolation, planning and checks before done, sourced from Paradev’s own docs.
summary: Polished worktree app for many CLI agents, MIT, macOS first. Formerly Superset.
answer: Paradev, formerly Superset, and Ninebrains both run CLI coding agents in parallel, one git worktree per task. Choose Paradev for a polished review and pull-request workflow, broad agent support and its mobile and remote features. Choose Ninebrains when you want a dependency-aware job graph and work that is blocked from counting as done until configured checks pass.
note: Paradev was previously named Superset, and its CLI command is still superset. It is unrelated to Apache Superset, the business intelligence tool.

what.text: A desktop app for running CLI coding agents in parallel, each task with its own git worktree, branch and terminals.

price.text: The desktop app is free. Paid plans, from $20 per user per month, add features such as automations.

platforms.text: macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel). Linux as an experimental AppImage. Windows is not yet available.

agents.text: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI, Cursor Agent, or any other CLI agent.

isolation.text: A git worktree per task. Their README notes worktrees separate working files and do not sandbox processes or prevent merge conflicts.

planning.text: A built-in chat with plan review. A task dependency graph is not described.

verification.text: Review tools: a Changes pane, a pull-request pane with checks and review threads, and a browser preview. You run the relevant tests yourself.

telemetry.text: Their privacy policy says usage data is processed by analytics providers such as PostHog. A statement specific to the desktop app was not found.

chooseThem.text: You want a polished review loop: diff, commit, pull request, checks and merge without leaving the app, plus a browser preview per worktree.
You run many different agents, or want an iPhone and iPad app, remote hosts or scheduled automations.

chooseUs: You want work planned as a graph of jobs with dependencies and handed to idle agents as it unblocks.
You want completion blocked until configured checks pass, with a reviewer that has read-only tools in a disposable checkout.
You need Windows support today, or want no telemetry at all.

faq.q: Is Paradev the same as Superset?
faq.a: Yes. Paradev’s README says it was previously named Superset and that the CLI command is still superset. It is unrelated to Apache Superset.
